content.value_statement: Complex TypeScript types can be hard to design, review, and maintain. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through safer advanced type patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains generics, constraints, conditional types, mapped types, and template literal types.
Provides reusable examples for typed events, API clients, builders, form validation, and state unions.
Shows type inference techniques using infer, type guards, assertion functions, and utility types.
Lists best practices for strict mode, unknown, interfaces, const assertions, and type tests.
Identifies pitfalls such as overusing any, weak null checks, and overly complex types.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not run TypeScript compilers or edit files by itself.
The API client example focuses on typing and uses a placeholder runtime implementation.
It does not cover every TypeScript release feature or framework-specific convention.
Complex examples may need changes for your tsconfig and compiler version.

use_cases.title: Design Package Types
use_cases.description: Create reusable public types for packages with generics, mapped types, and clear utility types.

use_cases.title: Model Application State
use_cases.description: Represent forms, events, and UI state with discriminated unions and compile-time checks.

use_cases.title: Tighten JavaScript Migrations
use_cases.description: Replace unsafe JavaScript shapes with strict TypeScript types during gradual migration.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Type Utility
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this TypeScript type in plain language. Show the input type, output type, and one safe use case: [paste type].

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Generic API
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this generic TypeScript API. Suggest safer constraints, better inference, and clearer utility types: [paste API].

prompt_templates.title: Design Typed Data Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design TypeScript types for this workflow. Include discriminated unions, validation errors, and typed events: [describe workflow].

prompt_templates.title: Audit Complex Types
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these advanced TypeScript types for correctness, performance risk, and maintainability. Recommend simpler alternatives where possible: [paste types].

output_examples.input: A developer asks for a type-safe event emitter design.
output: A typed event map for each event name.
Listener and emit signatures that enforce payload shapes.
Notes about avoiding any in public event payloads.

output_examples.input: A team needs safer form validation types.
output: A validation rule model tied to each form field.
Typed error output for each field.

output_examples.input: A library has slow recursive utility types.
output: A review of recursion depth and distribution risk.
Simpler alternatives using built-in utility types.
Type tests to protect expected behavior.

best_practices: Use strict compiler settings before relying on advanced type guarantees.
Keep reusable type utilities small, named, and covered by type tests.
Prefer unknown and type guards when data crosses runtime boundaries.
anti_patterns: Using any to bypass hard inference problems.
Creating deeply recursive types when a simple interface would work.
Treating compile-time types as runtime validation.

faq.question: Does this skill execute code?
faq.answer: No. It provides TypeScript guidance and examples. It does not run commands by itself.

faq.question: Can it help with type-safe APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for endpoint configs, request options, and response inference.

faq.question: Does it replace runtime validation?
faq.answer: No. TypeScript checks compile-time shapes. Use runtime validators for external data.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it useful for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. Start with generics and utility types before using conditional or recursive types.

faq.question: Can it reduce TypeScript compile time?
faq.answer: It can suggest simpler types. It cannot measure compile time without project tooling.
